key_insight: Temporal (causal) reasoning in video diffusion models can be separated from the multi-step denoising procedure: causal attention need not run at every layer and step and can be implemented as a lightweight, modular component.
problem_solved: Current causal diffusion models entangle temporal reasoning with iterative denoising—leading to high compute, tight coupling across layers/steps, and reduced modularity; this work shows how to decouple causality from denoising while preserving generation quality.
method: Introduce a separable causal module that encapsulates temporal (uni-directional) reasoning independent of the denoiser.
Apply causal attention sparsely (e.g., at select layers/steps or in a single pass) instead of across all layers and every denoising iteration.
Train/design the pipeline so the denoiser and causal module can operate modularly, maintaining sample quality with reduced computation and context entanglement.
impact: Makes video (and other temporally-structured) diffusion models more compute-efficient, scalable, and easier to transfer or adapt—beneficial for practitioners needing temporally coherent generative models with lower resource cost.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram: separate blocks for 'Causal Reasoning Module' and 'Denoiser' with arrows showing modular interaction.
Timeline/comparison: baseline (causal attention at every step) vs separable approach (causal applied sparsely) illustrating fewer attention invocations.
Bar/line chart: compute (FLOPs or latency) vs generation quality (temporal consistency / FID) showing similar or better quality at lower cost.
Example frames + attention maps: show temporal consistency maintained with the separable causal module.
paper_title: Causality in Video Diffusers is Separable from Denoising
paper_authors: Xingjian Bai, Guande He, Zhengqi Li, Eli Shechtman, Xun Huang
